get.description:
Liveness + capabilities + cascade readiness probe.

``status`` stays ``"ok"`` whenever the process is up — the HTTP code
is a *liveness* signal and a degraded cascade must not trigger a
restart (a crash-loop fixes neither a bad md file nor disk bloat).
The ``cascade`` block is the *readiness* signal: ``healthy=false``
with human-readable ``reasons`` **only** when the projection pipeline
itself is stuck (drain failing, optimize stuck, version cleanup
stalled). ``failed_permanent`` — files awaiting ``cascade fix`` — is
a data-quality backlog reported as an informational count that does
not flip ``healthy``. Alert on ``cascade.healthy``.
Render the current Prometheus registry in exposition format.

post.description:
Add messages into the user-memory + agent-memory pipelines.

``200`` means the markdown write was accepted. ``data.status`` of
``degraded`` is a failed index projection, not a different status code.

Drain the projection queue, then stop watcher + scanner + worker.

Returns when the index is a complete projection of the markdown on disk and
nothing further will rewrite it. That ordering is the point: stopping first
would freeze a *partial* index, which reads as a healthy store that quietly
fails to recall whatever had not been indexed yet.

Idempotent -- a second call reports ``quiesced=false`` rather than failing.

pending.title: Pending
pending.description: Unfinished queued batches of this session, this one included

AcceptedResponseData.title: AcceptedResponseData
AcceptedResponseData.description: 202 body: the batch is persisted and queued for the memorize worker.

status.title: Status
status.description: What this call did. HTTP 200 means the markdown write was accepted. `degraded` means the index projection of at least one file this call wrote failed (`failed_permanent` / `failed_retryable`). A file still queued when the call stops waiting is lag, not a failure, and leaves this `extracted`.

failed_permanent.title: Failed Permanent
failed_permanent.description: Files this call wrote whose index projection failed and will not be retried. Non-zero only when status is degraded.

failed_retryable.title: Failed Retryable
failed_retryable.description: Files this call wrote whose index projection failed and may still be retried. Non-zero only when status is degraded.

AddResponseData.title: AddResponseData
AddResponseData.description:
``200`` body. The status code means markdown was accepted.

Whether those files reached the index is ``status`` plus the failure
counts. ``degraded`` is not a different HTTP status.

index_rows.title: Index Rows
index_rows.description: Rows per business index table, counted once when the process started. A snapshot, not a live count: counting costs a round trip per collection on a remote backend and this endpoint is polled. `everos cascade status` counts live.

index_emptied.title: Index Emptied
index_emptied.description: True when the cascade ledger says every file is indexed, nothing is pending, and every index table is empty -- the state left behind by deleting the index directory, which the ledger in .index/sqlite survives. Searches return nothing while every other signal here reads healthy. Recover with `everos cascade rebuild`; markdown is untouched. Informational like failed_permanent: it does not flip `healthy`, because it is a startup snapshot that could not clear until a restart.

CascadeHealthBlock.title: CascadeHealthBlock
CascadeHealthBlock.description:
Readiness of the md → LanceDB projection (cascade) subsystem.

``healthy`` reflects **operational** health only — drain loop alive,
optimize not stuck, version cleanup (prune) not stalled — and is what
alerting should watch. ``failed_permanent`` (md files awaiting
``cascade fix``) is a normal data-quality backlog reported as an
informational count; it does **not** flip ``healthy``, otherwise the
signal would sit red forever.

ContentItemDTO.title: ContentItemDTO
ContentItemDTO.description: Content piece (v1 API brief appendix A).

DeleteByIdsRequest.title: DeleteByIdsRequest
DeleteByIdsRequest.description:
Episodes to delete, by memory id ``<owner_id>_<entry_id>``.

The whole request is rejected (422, nothing deleted) if any id is not an
episode id of a path-safe owner with a real date.

DeleteReason.title: DeleteReason
DeleteReason.description: Why the caller deletes: logged as ``code``; ``note`` is never logged.

DeleteRequest.title: DeleteRequest
DeleteRequest.description:
Which memories to delete: an owner, a session, or one owner's session.

At least one of ``user_id``, ``agent_id`` and ``session_id``; never both
``user_id`` and ``agent_id``.

DeleteResponseData.title: DeleteResponseData
DeleteResponseData.description:
What a deletion removed.

Attributes:
    filters: The scope fields the request set.
    count: Memories removed (entries, plus one per skill and one for the
        profile when a whole owner is deleted).

DocumentContextDTO.title: DocumentContextDTO
DocumentContextDTO.description: L1 document metadata attached to every search hit.

DocumentOverviewItemDTO.title: DocumentOverviewItemDTO
DocumentOverviewItemDTO.description: One row in the paginated document list.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error codes returned in the API error envelope.

Each code maps to exactly one HTTP status code. Clients can switch on
this value to decide retry / display / routing behaviour without parsing
the human-readable ``message`` field.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: Inner ``error`` object in the canonical error envelope.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Canonical error envelope returned by all error handlers.

FilterNode.title: FilterNode
FilterNode.description:
One Filters DSL node.

Recursive ``AND`` / ``OR`` arrays mix with arbitrary scalar fields at
the same level. Pydantic only checks the combinators; field-level
safety is enforced when compiling the node to a LanceDB ``where``
string in :mod:`everos.memory.search.filters`.

status.title: Status
status.description: What this flush did. HTTP 200 means the markdown write was accepted. `degraded` means the index projection of at least one file this flush wrote failed (`failed_permanent` / `failed_retryable`). A file still queued when the flush stops waiting is lag, not a failure, and leaves this `extracted`.

failed_permanent.title: Failed Permanent
failed_permanent.description: Files this flush wrote whose index projection failed and will not be retried. Non-zero only when status is degraded.

failed_retryable.title: Failed Retryable
failed_retryable.description: Files this flush wrote whose index projection failed and may still be retried. Non-zero only when status is degraded.

FlushResponseData.title: FlushResponseData
FlushResponseData.description:
``200`` body. The status code means markdown was accepted.

``degraded`` reports a failed index projection in the body. It does
not change the HTTP status.

GetAgentCaseItem.title: GetAgentCaseItem
GetAgentCaseItem.description: Agent case listing item — always agent-scoped.

GetAgentSkillItem.title: GetAgentSkillItem
GetAgentSkillItem.description: Agent skill listing item — always agent-scoped.

GetData.title: GetData
GetData.description:
Body of ``response.data``.

All four arrays are always present so client code can iterate
without branching on ``memory_type``; the route populates exactly
one.

GetMemoryType.title: GetMemoryType
GetMemoryType.description:
The four kinds enumerated by ``/get``.

``episode`` and ``profile`` are user-owned; ``agent_case`` and
``agent_skill`` are agent-owned. Cross-pairs are rejected by
:meth:`GetRequest._validate_owner_memory_type_pair`.

Naming note: all four values use the bare kind name (no
``_memory`` suffix) and match the LanceDB table name + everalgo
type name for that kind.

GetProfileItem.title: GetProfileItem
GetProfileItem.description: Owner profile — at most one per response, only for user owners.

GetRequest.title: GetRequest
GetRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v2/memory/get``.

Callers identify the memory owner via ``user_id`` XOR ``agent_id`` —
exactly one must be set. Internally the manager keeps using
``owner_id`` / ``owner_type`` (the storage tables' columns); those
are exposed as derived properties so the rename only affects the
wire contract.

embed.title: Embed
embed.description: Whether the embedding service answered the startup dimension probe. A snapshot taken when the process started, not a liveness check: a service that recovers later still reads false until the next restart.

HealthCapabilities.title: HealthCapabilities
HealthCapabilities.description:
Availability flags for the four capability probes.

Field order matches the health-endpoint payload contract; clients
key off these names to decide whether to expose optional features.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description:
Response schema for ``GET /health``.

Declared as a Pydantic model (not ``dict``) so the generated
OpenAPI schema carries the full field shape — ``capabilities``,
``disabled_features`` and ``cascade`` are typed. A bare ``-> dict``
return type degrades the OpenAPI response to
``additionalProperties: true``, which robs clients (and codegen) of
any structure to lean on.

defer_extraction.title: Defer Extraction
defer_extraction.description: Persist messages in the durable unprocessed buffer without running boundary detection or extraction. A later /flush commits the batch.

async_mode.title: Async Mode
async_mode.description: Persist the batch to the memorize queue and return 202 at once instead of running boundary detection and extraction inline. Poll GET /tasks/{request_id}. A session that already has queued batches is queued even when this is false, so batches never run out of order.

MemorizeQueueHealthBlock.title: MemorizeQueueHealthBlock
MemorizeQueueHealthBlock.description:
Readiness of the ``async_mode`` memorize queue.

``healthy`` is the delivery loop being alive. The probe only observes;
the loop relaunches itself (and on the next ``/add``), and
``loop_restarts`` counts how often that happened. ``pending`` and
``oldest_pending_age_s`` are the backlog: growing with a live loop means
delivery is slower than arrival (or the LLM is down), which is a
capacity signal, not a liveness one. Alert on ``healthy`` and on
``loop_restarts`` changing.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Message event time as Unix epoch in **milliseconds** (v1 API contract; the algo layer auto-detects sec vs ms for backward compat but the contract is ms).

QuiesceResponse.title: QuiesceResponse
QuiesceResponse.description:
What the final drain accomplished, and what it left behind.

``pending_before`` is the queue depth on arrival: a caller that expected the
projection to be up to date can assert it was 0 and learn otherwise. Anything
above 0 in ``pending_after`` means the drain could not finish -- the index is
NOT a complete projection of the markdown, and searching it will silently
under-recall.

RunSummary.title: RunSummary
RunSummary.description: One strategy run within a trigger response.

SearchAtomicFactItem.title: SearchAtomicFactItem
SearchAtomicFactItem.description: A single atomic fact nested inside its parent episode.

SearchData.title: SearchData
SearchData.description:
Body of ``response.data``.

All five arrays are always present so client code can iterate without
branching on ``owner_type``. Routes not applicable to the request's
owner type stay as ``[]``. ``unprocessed_messages`` is filled only
when ``filters.session_id`` is present as a top-level eq scalar —
in-flight buffer rows are scope-tagged but unattributed (no
``user_id``), so session is the only meaningful query dimension.

SearchEpisodeItem.title: SearchEpisodeItem
SearchEpisodeItem.description:
Episode hit — always user-scoped in the current emission contract.

``type`` is narrowed to ``"Conversation"`` because the only emitted
episode shape today is conversation-derived; widen when other
sources ship. Item kind is encoded by class name (no ``owner_type``
field on the wire), so episode results never carry ambiguity.

SearchHitDTO.title: SearchHitDTO
SearchHitDTO.description: One ranked result from knowledge search.

SearchMethod.title: SearchMethod
SearchMethod.description: Public method enum. RRF / LR / vector_anchored are hidden under HYBRID.

SearchProfileItem.title: SearchProfileItem
SearchProfileItem.description:
Owner profile — at most one per response, only for user owners.

``score`` is ``None`` for direct fetches (``include_profile=true``
on its own does no ranking); a future query-aware lookup may fill
it in.

enable_llm_rerank.title: Enable Llm Rerank
enable_llm_rerank.description: Opt-in LLM rerank pass for HYBRID. Applies to agent_case and agent_skill fusion only; the episode hybrid path has built-in fact eviction and ignores this flag. Ignored by keyword / vector / agentic.

SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest
SearchRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v2/memory/search``.

Callers identify the memory owner via ``user_id`` XOR ``agent_id`` —
exactly one must be set. Internally the manager + compile_filters keep
using ``owner_id`` / ``owner_type`` (the storage tables' columns);
those are exposed as derived properties so the rename only affects
the wire contract, not the internal recall plumbing.

TaskItem.title: TaskItem
TaskItem.description:
``GET /tasks/{task_id}`` -- one accepted request, in the Cloud's shape.

``id`` is the request id of the accepting call. Cloud also emits
``pending`` (accepted, boundary not run yet); this build never does, so a
client written for Cloud sees a subset of the statuses it already handles.

TopicOverviewDTO.title: TopicOverviewDTO
TopicOverviewDTO.description: Minimal topic summary inside a document detail.

TriggerResponse.title: TriggerResponse
TriggerResponse.description:
Response body for ``POST /api/v2/ome/trigger``.

``status`` distinguishes three outcomes that were previously masked as
a single ``ok``:

- ``ok``: at least one strategy was dispatched and all runs settled
  within ``timeout``. Individual run outcomes are in ``runs`` (a
  ``dead_letter`` there is still ``ok`` at this level — the strategy
  *ran*, it just failed permanently).
- ``timeout``: at least one strategy was dispatched but the engine did
  not go idle within ``timeout``. Runs may be partially complete;
  poll ``GET /health`` for cascade convergence separately.
- ``not_dispatched``: no strategy was dispatched — the subscriber was
  rejected by one of the dispatch gates (``_routes_to`` / ``enabled`` /
  ``applies_to`` / ``Counter``). Common cause: forgetting
  ``force=true`` on a strategy that is ``enabled=false`` in ome.toml.

UnprocessedMessageDTO.title: UnprocessedMessageDTO
UnprocessedMessageDTO.description:
A raw message still in the boundary-detection buffer.

No extracted memcell yet, no owner inference yet (attribution
happens at boundary detection). Returned by ``/search`` **only when**
``filters.session_id`` is present as a top-level eq predicate —
unprocessed messages have no ``user_id`` / ``agent_id`` to filter
on, so session is the only meaningful query dimension.
